Shared Storm

Goal: jarl-card (the static GitHub Pages business card with the ASCII tornado) becomes a shared world: every visitor's colored lightning strikes appear live for everyone else, and a global counter shows how many lightning strikes have EVER been fired. Barkpark is the entire backend.

Why a new plugin (decision)

Verified 2026-07-05: guerrilla's API returns no Access-Control-Allow-Origin headers — browsers cannot call /v1/data/* cross-origin. Tokens minted by token.create are read-only and workspace-bound (good for feed reads, useless for anonymous writes). The tickets plugin proves the pattern for low-trust outside writers (possession of a named key = identity) but its document shape (threaded request/answer) is wrong for high-volume tiny events. Therefore: a small first-party plugin, pulse — public, anonymous, rate-limited event ingest + durable counters + a cheap recent-events feed, with CORS handled explicitly on its own routes only. Generic by design: lightning strikes today; guestbooks, live cursors, reaction counters tomorrow. Rides the standard Barkpark.Plugin behaviour — with the plugin off, Barkpark is untouched.

Architecture

Barkpark side — plugin pulse

  • POST /v1/plugins/pulse/:channel/events — anonymous, CORS-open, rate-limited (per-IP token bucket + per-channel global cap). Body validated against the channel's declared event schema (for jarl-card: {hue: 0..359, x: 0..1, y: 0..1, mega: bool}, max ~200 bytes). Effect: insert one tiny pulse_event row/doc + atomically increment the channel's durable counter.
  • GET /v1/plugins/pulse/:channel/recent?since=<cursor> — anonymous, CORS-open. Returns events after the cursor (monotonic id), the total-ever counter, and the next cursor. Designed to be polled every 2–4 s by every open tab; must stay index-cheap.
  • GET /v1/plugins/pulse/:channel/stats — total ever, today, last hour.
  • TTL sweep: events older than ~24 h are deleted by an Oban cron (same pattern as the Tasks plugin sweep). The counter row is what persists forever — the feed is ephemeral, the count is durable.
  • Channel config (plugin settings): channel whitelist, event schema, rate limits, allowed origins. No channel = 404; nothing is open by default.

jarl-card side

  • On a user strike (button or cloud-click): fire-and-forget POST of {hue, x, y, mega}. Local rendering stays exactly as-is — the storm never waits on the network.
  • Poll recent every ~3 s; render other visitors' strikes as tinted bolts in their hue (extend the per-visit accent machinery to per-bolt hue). Others' strikes render slightly ghosted vs your own so presence reads without confusion.
  • Counter UI: a quiet ⚡ N line under CREATE LIGHTNING, ticking as the poll updates. The number is the number of strikes ever fired by anyone.
  • Offline grace: if Barkpark is unreachable the storm is simply local — no errors surface.

Abuse posture

Anonymous public write is the whole point, so the blast radius is capped instead: strict schema validation, tiny payload cap, per-IP bucket (e.g. 10/min burst 3), per-channel global ceiling (e.g. 5 000/day), events are ephemeral, counter increments are the only durable effect. Worst case a spammer inflates a vanity counter and briefly noises the feed — acceptable for v1; a named low-trust key (tickets-style) is the escalation path if needed.

Ops

Plugin lands in the barkpark repo via branch + PR (primary checkout stays on main), deploys to guerrilla via the standard CD pull. Channel jarl-card configured post-deploy; smoke = curl POST + recent from an Origin: https://frikkern.github.io preflight. Client ships to GitHub Pages as usual.

Open questions

  • Presence ("N watching") — cheap approximation via distinct poll cursors in the last minute; v2.
  • WebSocket/SSE instead of polling — only if polling load ever matters; the contract (cursor + recent) survives that swap.
